Landed on feat/sharing-primitives (pushed to origin). Five commits:

  bce9ccc feat(protocol): add Invitation, Grant types for sharing
  a6040ad feat(server): persist invitations + grants; add CRUD endpoints
  2b1a266 feat(server): grants relax authz decisions for object.read/write
  266aed6 feat(swift): add FrickClient sharing methods
  a1731e4 test(sharing): cover invitation + grant + authz

# Public API (Swift)

  extension FrickClient {
    public func createInvitation(
        recordType: String,
        recordId: String,
        permission: FrickSharingPermission,
        expiresIn: TimeInterval? = nil
    ) async throws -> FrickInvitation

    public func acceptInvitation(token: String) async throws -> FrickGrant

    public func listGrants(
        recordType: String? = nil,
        recordId: String? = nil,
        includeRevoked: Bool = false
    ) async throws -> [FrickGrant]

    @discardableResult
    public func revokeGrant(grantId: String) async throws -> FrickGrant
  }

  public enum FrickSharingPermission: String { case read, write }
  public struct FrickInvitation: Codable, Sendable, Identifiable { ... }
  public struct FrickGrant: Codable, Sendable, Identifiable { ... }

# Wire / HTTP

  POST   /share/invite        body: { recordType, recordId, permission, expiresInSeconds? }
                              -> 201 { invitation: FrickInvitation }
  POST   /share/accept        body: { token }
                              -> 201 { grant: FrickGrant }
  GET    /share/grants[?recordType=&recordId=&includeRevoked=]
                              -> 200 { grants: FrickGrant[] }
  DELETE /share/grants/:id    -> 200 { grant: FrickGrant }   (idempotent)

All routes require a session token. Default invitation TTL 14 days,
clamped to a 90-day server ceiling.

# How RangerCRM integrates

1. Owner-side "share" UI calls client.createInvitation(recordType:"Account",
   recordId:acct.id, permission:.write), then ships invitation.token to the
   recipient via any out-of-band channel (link in iMessage, push notif, QR,
   etc.) — Frick does not dictate the channel.

2. Recipient app calls client.acceptInvitation(token:) on tap of the share
   link's deep-link handler. The returned FrickGrant is durable; recipient
   can now read/write the underlying record subject to the policy hooks
   the RangerCRM server registers.

3. Owner-side "manage shares" UI calls client.listGrants(recordType:
   "Account", recordId: acct.id) to render current participants.
   Revocation = client.revokeGrant(grantId:).

4. For cascade ("share whole company -> all accounts shared"), iterate
   children on the client and createInvitation for each. The framework
   intentionally does not cascade — that's app-side.

5. RangerCRM's server-side FrickPolicyHook is what makes grants useful:
   tighten object.write on Account/Company so only the owner can write
   by default; the framework's grant relaxation then re-allows writes
   for valid grantees. Without a tightening hook, grants are a no-op
   (object.write already allows any authenticated tenant user).

# Limitations / things RCRM should know

- object.read is NOT in the framework's default decide() switch — list
  reads are tenant-scoped at the storage layer, not authz-gated per row.
  If RangerCRM needs row-level read gating, the new assertCanReadObject
  helper exists and accepts the same grantLookup, but you'll have to
  call it explicitly in your read paths or via a policy hook on
  projection.read.

- Cross-tenant sharing is rejected by design. If two RangerCRM users
  live in different tenants, sharing between them isn't possible until
  Frick gains a separate "external grant" concept.

- The framework does NOT notify a recipient that they have a pending
  invitation. Delivery of invitation.token is entirely the app's
  problem (push, link, etc.).

- Grantee-initiated "leave a share" is not exposed as DELETE
  /share/grants/:id today — only the owner can revoke. RangerCRM can
  layer its own "leave" surface (a thin app route that revokes on
  behalf of a grantee via the FrickStore).

# Tests

apps/server/tests/sharing.test.ts: 9 cases, all green. Full suite (790
passing) regression-clean. swift test on FrickSwift also green.
